Compare and contrast concepts and strategies to protect data
Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture

concepts.name: Cloud responsibility boundaries
concepts.description: Identify how security responsibilities are divided between an organization, cloud providers, and third parties.

concepts.name: Hybrid and third-party architecture
concepts.description: Recognize security implications created by hybrid environments and external service dependencies.

concepts.name: Infrastructure as code
concepts.description: Understand the security benefits and risks of defining infrastructure through versioned, automated configuration.

concepts.name: Serverless and microservices
concepts.description: Distinguish security implications of serverless functions and independently deployed microservices.

concepts.name: Network isolation and segmentation
concepts.description: Distinguish air gaps, logical segmentation, and software-defined networking.

concepts.name: Centralized and decentralized architecture
concepts.description: Compare security and operational tradeoffs of centralized and decentralized designs.

concepts.name: Containers and virtualization
concepts.description: Compare isolation boundaries and security considerations of containers and virtual machines.

concepts.name: IoT, ICS, SCADA, RTOS, and embedded systems
concepts.description: Recognize specialized systems whose safety, timing, lifecycle, or resource constraints affect security choices.

concepts.name: High availability architecture
concepts.description: Recognize architectural choices intended to keep services available through component failures.

concepts.name: Architecture security tradeoffs
concepts.description: Evaluate availability, resilience, cost, responsiveness, scalability, deployment, recovery, and risk-transference tradeoffs.

concepts.name: Patch, power, and compute constraints
concepts.description: Account for patch availability, inability to patch, power, and compute limitations when selecting security controls.

concepts.name: Device placement and security zones
concepts.description: Place security controls and systems in zones that reduce exposure and limit attack paths.

concepts.name: Attack surface and connectivity
concepts.description: Reduce unnecessary exposure by limiting reachable services, paths, and trust relationships.

concepts.name: Fail-open and fail-closed
concepts.description: Choose failure behavior based on security and availability requirements.

concepts.name: Active, passive, inline, and monitor-mode devices
concepts.description: Distinguish whether a security device observes, blocks, or sits directly in the traffic path.

concepts.name: Jump servers and proxy servers
concepts.description: Distinguish controlled administrative access points from intermediary client-service communication.

concepts.name: IDS and IPS
concepts.description: Distinguish detection-oriented monitoring from prevention that can block malicious traffic.

concepts.name: Load balancers and sensors
concepts.description: Recognize traffic distribution and telemetry collection roles in infrastructure security.

concepts.name: 802.1X and EAP
concepts.description: Understand port-based network access control and the authentication framework used with it.

concepts.name: Firewall types and inspection layers
concepts.description: Choose WAF, UTM, NGFW, Layer 4, or Layer 7 controls based on what must be inspected or protected.

concepts.name: VPN and remote access
concepts.description: Use encrypted tunnels and controlled remote access to protect communications over untrusted networks.

concepts.name: TLS and IPsec
concepts.description: Distinguish transport/application-session protection from network-layer IP security.

concepts.name: SD-WAN and SASE
concepts.description: Recognize software-defined WAN management and cloud-delivered networking/security convergence.

concepts.name: Infrastructure control selection
concepts.description: Select complementary controls that fit an infrastructure scenario without adding unnecessary exposure.

concepts.name: Data types
concepts.description: Recognize regulated, trade secret, intellectual property, legal, financial, human-readable, and non-human-readable data.

concepts.name: Data classification
concepts.description: Apply organization-defined sensitivity labels such as public, private, confidential, restricted, sensitive, and critical.

concepts.name: Data states
concepts.description: Distinguish data at rest, in transit, and in use.

concepts.name: Data sovereignty and geolocation
concepts.description: Understand how physical or legal location can affect data-handling requirements.

concepts.name: Encryption and hashing for data protection
concepts.description: Choose encryption for confidentiality and hashing for integrity-oriented verification.

concepts.name: Masking, tokenization, and obfuscation
concepts.description: Distinguish techniques that hide, substitute, or make sensitive information harder to interpret.

concepts.name: Data segmentation and permission restrictions
concepts.description: Limit who or what can reach sensitive data through isolation and access restrictions.

concepts.name: Load balancing and clustering
concepts.description: Distinguish traffic distribution from coordinated groups of systems used for availability and failover.

concepts.name: Hot, warm, and cold sites
concepts.description: Compare alternate recovery sites by readiness, cost, and time to resume operations.

concepts.name: Geographic and platform diversity
concepts.description: Use separation and diversity to reduce correlated failures while accounting for added complexity.

concepts.name: Multi-cloud and continuity of operations
concepts.description: Understand how provider diversity and continuity planning support sustained critical operations.

concepts.name: Capacity planning
concepts.description: Plan sufficient people, technology, and infrastructure capacity for normal operation and recovery.

concepts.name: Resilience testing
concepts.description: Distinguish tabletop, failover, simulation, and parallel-processing exercises.

concepts.name: Backup strategy
concepts.description: Evaluate backup location, frequency, encryption, snapshots, and recovery requirements.

concepts.name: Replication and journaling
concepts.description: Distinguish copied data/system state from recorded change histories used to support recovery.

concepts.name: UPS and generators
concepts.description: Use short-term battery power and longer-duration generation to maintain service during utility outages.
